newsitem.title: Australia: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: COSTELLO WELCOMES WAGE FIGURE
Federal Treasurer Peter Costello says today's wages figure, and yesterday's inflation figure, show the economy is on track.
Mr Costello's again called for restraint when enterprise bargaining agreements are being negotiated.

He says while it's up to the Reserve Bank to decide if interest rates should fall, today's quarterly survey is a good figure, given that it came in below the four per cent target the Government says is needed in order to achieve a cut in interest rates.
METAL INDUSTRY WORKERS DEFEND WAGE CLAIM
The Metal Trades Industry Association says a 15 percent wage claim by the Metal Workers' Union would contribute to unemployment, and send investment offshore.
The association's Bert Evans says manufacturing can't afford the two year claim.
But union secretary, Doug Cameron's defended the claim, saying the union's now operating in a market environment.
Mr Evans says the union's free to seek the best deal it can for its members, now that it's free from the accord.
He says the industry can't have both a decentralised system where market forces rule, and a de facto wage agreement developed voluntarily by the unions.
PROTEST AGAINST MOVES TO SACK COUNCIL
Adelaide's Lord Mayor, Henry Ninio, has led a march through the city to protest against State Government moves to sack the Adelaide City Council.
Mr Ninio says the bill to sack the council is undemocratic, and he will continue fighting the proposal.
Around 150 people joined Mr Ninio in the protest, which culminated in a rally on the steps of Parliament House.

The Local Government Association will also hold a rally at Parliament House tomorrow, calling on the state government to allow the elected members of the Adelaide City Council to serve their full term in office.
BAIL REFUSED FOR STUDENT STABBER
Bail has been refused for a fourteen-year-old boy charged with the attempted murder of a teacher at Marrickville High School in Sydney yesterday morning.
Police arrested the teenager at a pool hall, after he allegedly stabbed the 32-year-old teacher in the back, as he walked through the school grounds.
Bidura Children's Court heard most classes at the school were cancelled because teachers were afraid to go into classrooms on their own.
Magistrate, Daphne Kok, refused an application for bail for the safety of the alleged victim, who's in hiding.
The matter's been adjourned to late next month.
HOWARD SAYS WON'T RESPOND TO HANSON
Prime Minister, John Howard, sys he won't respond to Independent MP, Pauline Hanson, because he wants to keep the issue in perspective.
Mr Howard has called for all migrants to be treated with tolerance and says it's wrong to say Australia is being swamped by Asians.
Mr Howard's told radio 2UE, there's a danger of turning people into martyrs, and creating a situation where they attract unecessary levels of attention.
AMENDMENTS TO SIGNIFICANTLY ALTER BILL

West Australian Greens Senator, Dee Margetts, says the Federal Government's Workplace Relations bill is a code for pushing down workers' wages and conditions to make them competitive with developing countries.
The Greens have proposed more than eighty amendments to the legislation, to be debated in the Senate next week, which Senator Margetts says would alter the bill fundamentally.
Senator Margetts says the principal object of the act should be to prevent and settle industrial disputes, not promote international competitiveness.
SKASE FUNDING DECISION SOON
Attorney-General Daryl Williams says there should be a decision soon on whether the Government will resume funding the earch to recover assets from failed businessman Christopher Skase.
Mr Williams says he hopes to meet next week with the trustee for Mr Skase's creditors, Max Donnelly.
Earlier this month the Government rejected Mr Donnelly's latest funding application, based on the Inspector-General of bankruptcy's view that there were no reasonable prospects of success.
However the Prime Minister then intervened and called for the funding to be resumed.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
